dva-med-097.text: Seeking to reduce computer costs of Lambda without losing performance, a team evaluates migrating compatible functions to the arm64 architecture (Graviton). What is the expected gain and what care is needed?
options: Arm64 functions do not generate logs in CloudWatch
Cost per millisecond around 20% lower performance equal or better; it is necessary to validate that dependencies with native binary are compatible with ARM
Migration requires rewriting the code in Rust
Arm64 is free of charge for functions up to 1 GB
dva-med-097.explanation: Functions in Graviton2 cost ~20% less by duration with competitive performance; pure code (Python/Node/Java) usually migrates directly, but libraries with compiled binaries require build for arm64.
dva-med-097.hint: The chip of the house snakes ~20% less per millisecond — only check if your native binaries speak ARM.
optionRationales: Functions in Graviton2 cost ~20% less by duration with competitive performance; pure code (Python/Node/Java) usually migrates directly, but libraries with compiled binaries require build for arm64.
There is no gratuitousness by architecture — the gain is the price per GB-second reduced.
Supported runtimes continue to be the same — architecture changes by configuration, not language.
Logging works identically in both architectures.

dva-med-098.text: A high volume application needs to publish custom business metrics on each request, but the PutMetricData synchronous calls add latency and cost of API. What is the alternative? CloudWatch offers to emit metrics in scale without extra calls?
options: Record the metrics in a spreadsheet at S3
Customized metrics do not work in high volume
Embedded Metric Format (EMF): Save structured logs to format EMF and the CloudWatch automatically extract the metrics asynchronously
dva-med-098.explanation: With EMF, the metric travels within the already issued log (stdout)/CloudWatch Logs): no additional synchronous calls, with high cardinality available and raw events preserved for analysis.
dva-med-098.hint: The metric takes a ride in LOG already written — the CloudWatch the 'fishing' of the built-in format, without extra call.
optionRationales: With EMF, the metric travels within the already issued log (stdout)/CloudWatch Logs): no additional synchronous calls, with high cardinality available and raw events preserved for analysis.
Duplicate cost and latency double calls — the opposite of the sought optimization.
Bucket files didn't see alarm metrics from CloudWatch — outside the monitoring ecosystem.
They function — or EMF there is exactly for the high volume and low overhead path.

dva-med-099.text: Tasks of a service ECS are being closed repeatedly right after the climb, and the service never stabilizes. What are the first places to investigate the cause of interruptions?
options: The bill of the account, because tasks stop for lack of payment
Delete cluster and recreate from zero immediately
The 'stopped reason' of the closed tasks (console/describe-tasks), the container logs in CloudWatch and service event history (health check failure, memory failure, image pull error))
The number of tags in the task definition
dva-med-099.explanation: The ECS records the reason for stopping each task (OutOfMemory, failure of ELB health check, CannotPullContainer) and service events narrate the cycle — combined with container logs, close the diagnosis.
dva-med-099.hint: Each closed task leaves a "stopped reason" — read it at service logs and events.
optionRationales: The ECS records the reason for stopping each task (OutOfMemory, failure of ELB health check, CannotPullContainer) and service events narrate the cycle — combined with container logs, close the diagnosis.
Recreate without diagnosis repeats the problem — the cause is recorded in the reasons for stopping and logs.
Suspension for collection would affect the entire account with warnings — not individual loop tasks.
Tags are metadata — don't influence task life cycle.

dva-med-100.text: A function Lambda critical need for visibility beyond standard metrics: real memory usage, CPU, network and cold start by running, with dashboards ready. Which feature provides this deep telemetry of functions?
options: The standard metrics already show memory usage per execution
Install a monitoring agent via SSH in function
CloudWatch Lambda Insights, enabled by layer/extension, collecting system metrics and invocation performance
dva-med-100.explanation: The Lambda Insights adds system level telemetry (real memory, CPU, network, init duration) with dedicated dashboards — revealing, for example, memory overlocation and cold start costs.
dva-med-100.hint: The 'inner X-ray' of functions: true memory, CPU and cold start, via observability layer.
optionRationales: The Lambda Insights adds system level telemetry (real memory, CPU, network, init duration) with dedicated dashboards — revealing, for example, memory overlocation and cold start costs.
Native metrics cover invocations, errors, duration, and throttles — real memory usage/CPU requires Insights (or parsing of REPORT).
No accessible server in the Lambda — additional telemetry enters by extension/managed layer.
The Trusted Advisor evaluates good account practices — does not monitor individual performance of functions.
